name: LTP primed burst, left temporal lobe, 3 x 5 min on, 5 min off (Persinger 1994)
origin: Persinger, Richards & Koren (Laurentian University), 1994 double-blind pleasantness study, left-hemisphere arm
summary: The left-hemisphere arm of Persinger, Richards & Koren (1994): a 1 uT 'LTP' pattern (a 2-ms primer, then four 2-ms pulses 150 ms later) mainly over the left temporal lobe, 5 min on and 5 min off three times. In their double-blind study (10 people per arm) the paper reports that this arm was rated less pleasant than the right arm.
notes: The pattern was a 2-ms primer followed 150 ms later by four 2-ms pulses 10 ms apart. The helmet had four solenoids per side, each left-right pair on for 10 s. The method describes 5 min on and 5 min off with 15 min of field in 30 min; the abstract and Table 1 say 20 min (Persinger 1994 p.2 [192]). The paper says only that the field was 'applied primarily over' one lobe. The repeat rate, 'the LTP pulse once every 4 s', and the other side's share, a tenth (1 mG against 10 mG), are from the companion study with the same helmet (Richards 1996 p.3 [143]). This program plays 2-ms pulses starting at 0, 150, 162, 174 and 186 ms, then a 4-s pause, for 5 min on and 5 min off three times, with the right side at a tenth of the left. It is rebuilt from the description: '10 msec' is read as the gap between pulses, end to start, and the positive-only pulses follow a later lab drawing (Corradini 2014 Fig. 2, p.103 [92]). One left-right pair is on at a time (10 s each), and the right side is reversed so that the pair's field points through the head. The four sites per side stand for the lab helmet's four solenoids per side on a 7.5 by 5 cm ellipse; the site names are this project's reading. Field: 1 uT, with no place given; the companion study gives 10 mG (1 uT) at 'the distance that would have been within the skull' (p.3 [143]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Result (Table 1, p.3 [193]): sham +0.9, both +0.8, left +0.1, right +1.2, 10 people each; only left and right differed. One lab, not repeated elsewhere. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Use the app's Blind option for the sham arm. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Seated or reclined in a quiet, dark room with the eyes covered (the lab's standard: blindfold or opaque goggles in an acoustic chamber). Rate how pleasant the session was before unblinding.
schedule: One session per person in the original (between-subjects): 5 min on and 5 min off, three times. For a self-test, compare the four arms (right, left, both, sham) in blinded, counterbalanced order on separate days.
source: Persinger, Richards & Koren 1994, Differential ratings of pleasantness following right and left hemispheric application of low energy magnetic fields that stimulate long-term potentiation, Int J Neurosci 79:191-197 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/7744561/ ; Corradini 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (LTP file: primer, then 4 pulses 150 ms later, 1-ms points, positive values) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/1455e1f3-2f1d-47b5-93cd-23713d69e651 ; Persinger 2010, The Harribance effect as pervasive out-of-body experiences, NeuroQuantology 8(4):444-465 (LTP: a single pulse, then about 170 ms later 4 pulses at 100-200 Hz) http://web.archive.org/web/20150426091303id_/http://www.neuroquantology.com/index.php/journal/article/download/301/346 ; Rose, Diamond, Pang & Dunwiddie 1988, Primed burst potentiation (as cited by Corradini 2014) ; Delparte & Persinger 2007, Int J Neurosci 117:295 (1 s pulse of 5 trains, continuous or with 5 s or 10 s ISI) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17365115/ ; McKay & Persinger 2005 (theta-burst, 200-500 nT, 4000 ms ISI) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15823929/ ; Richards, Persinger & Koren 1996, Electro- and Magnetobiology 15:141 (a 1 uT field structure that promotes long-term potentiation in hippocampal slices) https://doi.org/10.3109/15368379609009830 ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
